citations.narrative:
The facility has sections of the perimeter fence that do not meet the requirements. Two enclosures housing a Southern
Three Banded Armadillo and a Larger Hairy Armadillo are located approximately 6 inches from the perimeter fence.
Failure to provide an appropriate distance between an enclosure and the perimeter fence may allow persons or other
animals to interact with the regulated animals.
All outdoor housing facilities must be enclosed by a perimeter fence that is of sufficient height to keep animals and
unauthorized person out. Fences less than 8 feet high (96 inches) for potentially dangerous animals, such as but not
limited to, large felines (e.g., lions, tigers, leopards, cougars, etc.), bears, wolves, rhinoceros, and elephants, or less than
6 feet high for other animals must be approved in writing by the Administrator. The fence must be constructed so that it
protects the animals in the facility by restricting animals and unauthorized persons from going through it or under it and
having contact with the animals in the facility, and so that it can function as a secondary containment system for the
animals in the facility. It must be of sufficient distance from the outside of the primary enclosure to prevent physical
contact between animals inside the enclosure and animals or persons outside the perimeter fence. Such fences less than
3 feet in distance from the primary enclosure must be approved in writing by the Administrator. Correct by ensuring that all
species requiring a perimeter fence are completely enclosed within an adequate perimeter fence that meets all
requirements. Alternatively, a variance may be requested in writing and sent to the APHIS Administrator. Correct by 7-
AUG-2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with a Facility Representative.
